title: A stretch window trimmed by less than a frame links instead of being refused

needles: The converse is deliberately not asserted, because it is not true.
Ticks resolve far finer than frames

installed_sdk.rationale: link_audio_track_program is an installed entry point and the only caller of the clip validator this narrows, so an SDK consumer that compiles a windowed stretch clip and links it is exactly who the refusal reached. No signature, type or error code changes: the same call now returns a track program where it returned InvalidAsset, so there is nothing new for a consumer to discover and nothing that reports in advance which trims a window tolerates. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: No CLI verb trims a nested placement or reports the frame window a trim resolves to, so an author cannot ask whether a trim falls below one frame and cannot reach the widened acceptance except by compiling a document that already carries it. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: The generated Timeline MCP schema carries no operation that trims a nested placement or exposes a stretch artifact's window, so the widened acceptance is not reachable there. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).

live_product_control.rationale: Product A live timeline authority is absent for the sequencer generally, so neither the trim nor the window it resolves to is reachable as a live control. Owner: NW-D, and only where that source is Pulp-owned.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: No agent-capability row states how a stretch window relates to the ticks it covers, so an agent authoring a trim cannot ask whether the trim is representable in frames before making it. Owner: NW-D (P0-40-CONTROLS).
